thread:
emma_support: FYI AcmePayments escalation — their EU customers are getting routed to our us-west POP, causing p99 spikes and a bunch of 401s/429s. They see auth failures and billing discrepancies because tokens are validated in the wrong region. Can net/DNS/infra take a look?

raj_netops: can you paste a sample client IP + the dig/resolve output from a failing customer network? also include any edge headers from a failing request.

emma_support: sample IP 85.214.33.18 (customer's office in DE). here's what they sent:

```\n$ dig +short @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.example.com
34.120.66.12
# from their resolver (google) resolves to a us-pop IP
\n$ curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate
< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized\n
# they also saw token accepted then 429s when routed; latency ~420ms
```\n\nand edge header snippet from their failing req:
```\nx-redwood-pop: us-west2\nx-redwood-pop-original: unknown\nx-client-ip: 85.214.33.18
```

liz_engineer: looks like EDNS/Resolver behavior — the resolver the customer uses is stripping ECS so GeoIP sees the query as coming from a Google/Cloudfront resolver range that maps to us-west. That + our fallback policy (if eu pool at cap) will send traffic to us-west. Also possible geoip DB still mapping that resolver net to us-west from older DB.

mike_infra: will check pool capacity and fallback triggers. can someone grep the edge logs for that client IP around the timestamps? also we should check which GeoIP DB version was active.

emma_support: pasted a few log lines they captured (anonymized):
```\n[2025-11-03T14:12:23Z] req_id=abc123 client_ip=85.214.33.18 pop=us-west2 route=default model=cli-1 status=401 latency=412ms
[2025-11-03T14:12:28Z] req_id=abc124 client_ip=85.214.33.18 pop=us-west2 route=fallback status=429 latency=430ms
```\n
dns-bot: geoip-db: v2025-09-28 currently active, last sync 2025-11-01 03:12:44 UTC

raj_netops: two things to run from a box in DE (or ask customer to run):
```\n# check what resolver returns from their network
dig @85.214.33.1 +short api.redwood.example.com
\n# check EDNS client subnet behavior
dig +short +edns=1 @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.example.com
dig +short @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.example.com
```\nAlso will run probes from our EU resolvers to see if responses differ. If the customer's local resolver is stripping ECS the authoritative view will see the resolver net.

liz_engineer: mitigation options: 1) add a temporary region-pin for AcmePayments (pin to eu-west) via routing policy; 2) force-use ECS-aware upstreams for their traffic; 3) schedule a geoip-db refresh and prefill caches for the resolver prefixes in question. I recommend 1+3 as fastest.

mike_infra: created infra ticket INF-2025-3277 to increase eu pool cap and apply temporary routing pin for customer; I'll coordinate with oncall. ETA 30m for pin, 2h for capacity bump.

emma_support: applied the temporary pin via console -> routing -> pins (customer: acme-payments, pin: eu-west). Customer reports after ~2m their p99 dropped to ~45ms and 401s stopped. Warning: their resolver TTLs might keep cached wrong answers for up to 10m.

raj_netops: followups: schedule a GeoIP DB refresh (dns-bot noted v2025-09-28, we should push v2025-11-15), run prefill probes against popular ISPs in DE/FR/NL and add them to our prefills list. Also add an alert if a single external resolver subnet causes >20% of cross-region routing.

liz_engineer: agree. after capacity changes and geoip refresh we'll remove the pin and monitor for 24h. please add a short postmortem: root cause (resolver strips ECS + outdated geoip mapping + fallback policy thresholds) and mitigation (prefill, geoip refresh cadence, routing pinning runbook).

emma_support: thanks all — I'll update AcmePayments and keep the thread open while we monitor. :thumbsup:
